title: Backend orphan-manifest repair can report success while producing a manifest the PowerShell drain must reject
observed_behavior: The Python pending manifest contract accepts a current pending_push_manifest.v1 without output_sha256 or output_hash_algorithm, and orphan reconcile validates that contract, writes the manifest, and returns applied=true. The PowerShell drain contract requires both fields and classifies the same manifest OUTPUT_HASH_MISSING, so the repaired payload remains parked. The repository integration test reproduced this exact split twice: the strict repair apply passed, the drain process returned 0, and the expected final output did not exist.
expected_invariant: Any backend repair/reconcile result advertised as a current drainable pending manifest must satisfy the same mandatory byte-proof contract enforced by the consuming PowerShell drain, and an end-to-end repair-then-drain test must pass.
root_cause: The Python dataclass models output hash fields as optional backward-compatible additions, while the PowerShell current-contract validator recently made SHA-256 proof mandatory for automatic drain. The repair producer reuses only the weaker Python contract and does not compute or require the stronger proof.
failure_scenario: An operator or future production proposal source repairs an orphan pending payload. The Local API returns a successful, strictly journaled apply and writes a schema-valid manifest, but the next drain silently leaves it queued as invalid_manifest/OUTPUT_HASH_MISSING. The operator sees a successful repair without the promised recovery outcome and must diagnose cross-language contract drift.
evidence: pending_publish.py lines 144-152 validates hash syntax only when output_sha256 is present; absence of both fields is accepted.
apply.py lines 321-347 validates the proposed manifest with PendingPushManifest.from_mapping and writes it without adding byte proof.
pending_manifest_store.ps1 lines 356-363 rejects a blank output_sha256 and requires output_hash_algorithm=SHA256.
The targeted 191-test recovery suite ended 190 passed/1 failed at the final output assertion, and an isolated rerun failed identically.
PendingPushManifest.from_mapping accepted the written test manifest before the PowerShell drain refused it, proving the split is between current authoritative consumers rather than malformed JSON.
affected_flows: Pending Publish orphan payload reconcile dry-run/apply
strict Local API repair command success reporting
operator recovery from orphaned parked output
existing_safeguards: PowerShell drain fails closed before copying or revealing bytes when SHA-256 proof is absent.
Repair apply requires confirm_apply=true, an exact dry-run fingerprint, candidate-only selection, exact pending-root path checks, and strict command journal durability.
The end-to-end integration test preserves source/payload hashes while checking repair and drain.
safeguard_gap: The fail-closed drain prevents unsafe publication but does not prevent the upstream repair service from declaring success and materializing a non-drainable current manifest. The Python contract and repair dry-run cannot tell the operator that required byte proof is absent.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_repair_reconcile_dry_run.py exercises injected backend manifest proposals through the Python contract.

tests/python/desktop/test_repair_reconcile_apply.py::RepairReconcileApplyTests::test_local_api_orphan_apply_then_pipeline_drain_publishes_payload covers strict apply followed by the actual bundled PowerShell drain.
tests_missing: Cross-language contract parity test asserting every Python-accepted current pending manifest passes the PowerShell current-contract validator.
Repair dry-run negative test for a proposal without output_sha256/output_hash_algorithm.
Backend proposal test that derives SHA-256 from exact payload bytes and binds sidecar hashes before apply.
recommended_remediation: Make the canonical pending manifest contract require output_sha256 and output_hash_algorithm=SHA256 for every newly written/current auto-drainable manifest, while modeling legacy scan-only records separately. Have the trusted backend proposal producer compute and bind hashes from exact payload/sidecar bytes, reject hashless repair candidates before apply, and keep the PowerShell fail-closed check. Update the integration fixture to carry real hashes and require repair-then-drain success.
remediation_risk: High: weakening the PowerShell hash requirement would reopen unsafe or ambiguous publication. Strengthening Python validation must preserve legacy scan visibility without incorrectly making old manifests repairable.
validation_rung: Targeted Python contract/dry-run/apply tests, PowerShell pending safety and transaction fault injection, cross-language contract parity, and representative synthetic park/repair/drain with unchanged source bytes. Real-media validation is advisable before release because final placement policy is affected.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from prior CSW-2026-07-09-PENDING-003: that finding covers absence of a production orphan proposal producer; this current defect reproduces even when a proposal is injected because the accepted proposal contract is weaker than the drain consumer.

title: Pending-manifest trust emits three operational reason codes absent from the outcome registry
observed_behavior: The current registry check fails because OUTPUT_HASH_MISSING, SIDECAR_HASH_INVALID, and SIDECAR_SIZE_INVALID are emitted by pending-manifest trust validation but are not present in the 215-code outcome registry. Consequently they have no canonical family, stage, retryability, severity, handler, trigger, or operator action row.
expected_invariant: Every operational reason/error code emitted into pending state, drain results, logs, failure records, or operator-visible status must have exactly one canonical outcome metadata row, and the registry check must be green.
root_cause: Stronger pending-manifest hash/sidecar contract branches were added without updating Get-MediaPipelineKnownOutcomeCodes and its metadata classifiers in the same change.
failure_scenario: A current manifest is hashless or contains an invalid sidecar proof. Drain correctly fails closed, but backend/operator tooling consuming the registry cannot classify the reason consistently, and the repository registry gate remains red.
evidence: Invoke-FailureCodeRegistryChecks.ps1 exited 1 with exactly: OUTPUT_HASH_MISSING, SIDECAR_HASH_INVALID, SIDECAR_SIZE_INVALID.
pending_manifest_store.ps1 emits the three codes at lines 359, 389, and 394 (with another SIDECAR_HASH_INVALID branch at line 467).
Get-MediaPipelineKnownOutcomeCodes returns 215 unique rows and contains OUTPUT_HASH_INVALID but none of the three failed-check codes.
The worker map records the three emissions separately from the 215 registered outcomes so they are not silently lost.
affected_flows: Pending Publish current-contract validation and drain status
failure/outcome operator guidance and recovery mapping
registry unit gate and generated diagnostic consumers
repair/reconcile handling of hash and sidecar proof failures
existing_safeguards: The pending drain itself fails closed and retains manifest/payload evidence.
The emitted-code registry check detects these three currently visible prefixes.
Pending safety and transaction fault-injection suites passed.
safeguard_gap: Runtime safety is retained, but canonical metadata and auditability are absent, and the authoritative registry test is red. The check also has separate blind spots documented in AUDIT-FIND-W15-004.
tests_missing: Explicit metadata assertions for all pending trust reason codes.
Parity test deriving emitted codes from result contracts rather than a partial token-prefix heuristic.
Operator read-model test proving each pending trust code resolves to guidance and retryability.
recommended_remediation: Register all three codes with publish family/stage, PendingManifestStore ownership, explicit retry/review semantics, and operator actions; then make the emitted-code inventory derived or comprehensive and rerun the registry, pending safety, and repair/drain tests.
remediation_risk: Low-to-medium for metadata addition, but retryability must match the trust boundary: missing or invalid proof must not become automatically retryable without a trusted repair step.
validation_rung: Failure-code registry check, pending safety/fault-injection tests, pending preview/operator-guidance tests, and the repair-then-drain integration path.
prior_audit_relationship: No matching current-hash registry-completeness finding was found in prior audit fragments; this was reproduced directly against the current registry and pending manifest store.

title: Seven shared failure/outcome codes resolve to conflicting canonical metadata
observed_behavior: Of the 46 codes shared by both registries, seven have namespace-dependent metadata. ENCODER_UNAVAILABLE, OUTPUT_DISK_FULL, FFMPEG_FAILED, FFMPEG_INVALID_ARGUMENT, FFMPEG_STOPPED, FFMPEG_TIMEOUT, and SYSTEM_OUT_OF_MEMORY disagree on family; the FFMPEG/SYSTEM group also disagrees on stage and handler, and several triggers differ.
expected_invariant: A code used as the join key between failure records, ProcessFileResult, runtime outcomes, operator guidance, and recovery tooling must have one namespace-independent semantic identity wherever it appears.
root_cause: Failure metadata and outcome metadata call separate family classifiers for the same shared code. Stage, handler, and default trigger are then derived from that divergent family, while the registry test checks only presence/nonblank fields and subset membership, not shared-code parity.
failure_scenario: The same FFMPEG_TIMEOUT record is grouped as native_tool/native-tool/NativeProcessContracts on a failure surface and generic_failure/generic-failure/FailureState on an outcome surface. Aggregation, severity dashboards, handler ownership, and recovery routing keyed by code can disagree depending on which registry was queried.
evidence: A read-only registry join found seven mismatched shared codes out of 46.
FFMPEG_FAILED and FFMPEG_INVALID_ARGUMENT differed in family, stage, trigger, and handler; FFMPEG_STOPPED and FFMPEG_TIMEOUT differed in family, stage, and handler.
ENCODER_UNAVAILABLE differed native_tool versus encode; OUTPUT_DISK_FULL differed output versus publish; SYSTEM_OUT_OF_MEMORY differed native_tool/native-tool versus generic_failure/generic-failure.
The current registry test has no assertion comparing metadata values for the shared failure-code subset.
affected_flows: runtime outcome grouping and operator guidance
telemetry or dashboards aggregating by code/family/stage
existing_safeguards: Both registries contain all 46 classifier failure codes.
Each individual row has nonblank trigger, handler, severity, and operator action.
Retryability and operator severity happen to agree for the seven mismatches.
safeguard_gap: Completeness alone does not establish semantic parity. A consumer has no supported way to know which namespace metadata is canonical for a shared code.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-FailureCodeRegistryChecks.ps1 checks failure subset membership and per-row nonblank metadata.
Worker-15 performed an exact field-by-field read-only join across all shared codes.
tests_missing: Shared-code parity assertion across Family, Stage, WhenFires, Retryable, OperatorSeverity, HandledBy, and OperatorAction.
Consumer test joining failure markers and runtime outcomes by code without namespace-dependent regrouping.
recommended_remediation: Define one metadata constructor/table for every code and have both registries reference it. If a code truly needs context-specific instances, model context as a separate field rather than changing the code's family/stage/owner. Add exact shared-subset parity coverage.
remediation_risk: Medium: dashboards or existing consumers may rely on current namespace-specific grouping. Choose and document canonical semantics before migrating.
validation_rung: Registry unit checks, failure marker/runtime outcome join tests, queue/operator guidance projection tests, and telemetry grouping validation.
prior_audit_relationship: No prior finding with the same shared-code metadata root cause was found in the current audit fragments.

title: The emitted-code registry scan misses registered prefix families and snake_case error fields
observed_behavior: The scan uses a hand-written prefix alternation that omits current families such as DYNAMIC, DOVI, DESTINATION, and LOCAL, and its line prefilter recognizes ErrorCode/errorCode but not snake_case error_code or reason_code. OUTPUT_MEDIA_TRACK_VERIFICATION_FAILED is emitted in a snake_case error_code field, returned into Register-SourceFailure by encode/remux verification, and absent from the registry, yet the registry check does not report it.
expected_invariant: The registry gate must detect every top-level operational code emitted by supported source conventions and must not require maintainers to remember a second incomplete prefix and field-name registry.
root_cause: The test approximates the code universe with two manually maintained regular expressions rather than deriving candidates from registry prefixes plus all result/failure field spellings or using structured contract constructors.
failure_scenario: The three currently reported pending codes are registered and the gate turns green, while OUTPUT_MEDIA_TRACK_VERIFICATION_FAILED or a future DYNAMIC_HDR/LOCAL_WORKER/DESTINATION_NAMING code remains unregistered. Operator tooling then receives an unknown fail-closed reason despite a passing registry gate.
evidence: The prefix probe did not match DYNAMIC_HDR_NEW_UNREGISTERED, DOVI_NEW_UNREGISTERED, DESTINATION_NAMING_NEW_UNREGISTERED, or LOCAL_WORKER_NEW_UNREGISTERED, while it matched OUTPUT_NEW_UNREGISTERED.
Line 103 prefilter omits error_code; media_track_verification.ps1 line 246 uses exactly that spelling.
The current outcome registry contains OUTPUT_MEDIA_TRACK_PROBE_FAILED/INVALID but not OUTPUT_MEDIA_TRACK_VERIFICATION_FAILED.
Invoke-MediaTrackOutputVerificationChecks.ps1 passed the fail-closed behavior, demonstrating the operational branch is live even though registry enforcement misses its code.
affected_flows: dynamic-HDR, destination naming, and local-worker future code additions
existing_safeguards: The media-track verifier returns allowed=false and encode/remux verification blocks publish.
A broad emitted-code scan exists and currently catches several conventional prefixes.
Per-row registry metadata completeness is checked after registration.
safeguard_gap: Fail-closed runtime behavior protects media, but the enforcement test can falsely certify registry completeness and leave operator/telemetry consumers with an unknown code.
tests_missing: Negative self-test fixtures for every current registry prefix and ErrorCode/errorCode/error_code/ReasonCode/reason_code spelling.
Assertion that OUTPUT_MEDIA_TRACK_VERIFICATION_FAILED is registered and metadata-complete.
Structured emitted-code inventory independent of raw source-line regex.
recommended_remediation: Register OUTPUT_MEDIA_TRACK_VERIFICATION_FAILED, then replace the hard-coded scan with a structured emitted-code inventory or at minimum derive prefixes from the registry and recognize every supported field spelling. Add negative fixtures that inject an unknown code for DYNAMIC, DOVI, DESTINATION, LOCAL, and snake_case result fields and require the gate to fail.
remediation_risk: Low-to-medium: a broader raw-token scan can create false positives for local/internal reason constants, so prefer typed result constructors or an explicit distinction between top-level outcomes and subordinate reason codes.
validation_rung: Registry check self-tests, media-track verification checks, encode/remux verification tests, and operator outcome projection tests.
prior_audit_relationship: No prior finding with this emitted-code scanner blind-spot root cause was found in current audit fragments.
